prompt: Write 5 short claim log entries by an auto insurance adjuster for a hit while turning left claim. Injury: neck and back strain. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1157; do not mention it.)
text:
Entry 1: Claim opened following report of a collision at an intersection involving a left turn. Insured vehicle was turning left when it struck a vehicle traveling straight through. Claimant reports neck and back strain and states she was seen at urgent care. Claimant is not represented by counsel. Requested police report and photos of both vehicles.

Entry 2: Spoke with claimant by phone. She describes stiffness in the neck and lower back, with pain worsening after sleeping. She has not yet received a diagnosis beyond soft tissue strain. Explained the claims process and that she may submit medical bills for review. Asked her to send treatment records when available.

Entry 3: Reviewed the police report. The responding officer cited the insured driver for failure to yield during a left turn. Scene diagram is consistent with the claimant's account of the vehicle path. Witness statement on file supports the claimant's version that the oncoming vehicle had the right of way. Liability appears clear against our insured at this stage.

Entry 4: Received photos of the claimant's vehicle showing rear door damage and a cracked taillight. Repair estimate requested from preferred shop. Claimant indicated she has not retained an attorney and asked whether she should. Advised her that she is free to seek independent advice and that I can only discuss the claim handling process with her.

Entry 5: Medical records received from urgent care reflecting diagnosis of cervical and lumbar strain, with muscle relaxants and physical therapy referral. Claimant reports she is attending therapy twice weekly. No surgery recommended at this time. Reserve adjusted to reflect ongoing treatment. Will follow up in thirty days for updated status and therapy progress.
